newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen denies Cambodia coup, says Ranariddh can return.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen denies Cambodia coup, says Ranariddh can return.

text.p: Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen denied on Thursday he had launched a coup d'etat, saying his ousted co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh could return to the country but would face trial if he did.

"It is not a coup d'etat. If I made a coup d'etat I would change the monarchy to a republic, suspend the constitution and arrest FUNCINPEC (royalist) ministers, but everything is still the same," he told reporters, referring to Ranariddh's royalist political party.
Ranariddh was overthrown on Sunday after two days of heavy fighting in the capital. The prince had left Cambodia for France two days earlier.
"I did not expel Ranariddh. Ranariddh fled by himself," Hun Sen said. "I will not invite him to return but I will not ban him from coming back. Ranariddh can come back to face court."

Hun Sen did not elaborate on what court proceedings Ranariddh would face but has said on a number of occasions that the prince should be put on trial for illegally negotiating with Khmer Rouge guerrillas and over allegations he tried to smuggle arms and ammunition into Cambodia.
Ranariddh has denounced his ouster as a coup d'etat and said he would organise resistance to Hun Sen's government.
Hun Sen said such an effort could not reverse the prince's situation, however.

"If Ranariddh establishes a resistance movement abroad, it is his right. But Ranariddh cannot resist the government. This government cannot be dissolved by Ranariddh and foreigners," he told reporters.
"Don't risk military action with me," he said.
He said the international community, which has expressed concern over the turmoil in Cambodia, should stay out of his country's affairs.
"I cannot please foreigners all the time, but I have to please my own people. I urge all foreigners to be cautious with what they are going to decide for Cambodia," Hun Sen said.

He also told members of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) to also stay out of Cambodia's business. He was speaking just minutes before sources in the grouping said the regional club opted to postpone his country's scheduled entry in July.
